title: B4 follow-on: completion double-key, drift mandrel wording and duplicate fixes

items.flag: distractor 0 (drift table from the specification) arguably true
items.reason: The drift table is independent of the equipment rows, so under the old prompt it was also correct; prompt sharpened to the lesson wording (depends on none of the catalog: pipe tables or equipment), which leaves only the space out.

prompt.old: Which calculation in this course is completely independent of the equipment catalog?
prompt.new: Which calculation in this course depends on none of the catalog at all, neither the API pipe tables nor the approximate equipment rows?

items.correct_change_reason: Correct option text unchanged; the prompt was sharpened so the drift table (which depends on the API pipe tables) no longer also qualifies.

items.flag: distractor 1 (every component same bore) arguably correct
items.reason: With a uniform bore the extreme equals the extent and the headline is a complete summary, so option 1 was defensible; replaced with reaching a depth above the restriction, where the lesson says the running minimum is the right number.

1.old: When every component in the string has the same bore throughout.
1.new: When the tool only has to reach a depth above the smallest bore.

items.flag: distractor 2 only wrong under this tier framing
items.reason: The setting-depth distractor is genuinely right when a liner governs; prompt now gives the drift of the single string the packer runs through, and option 2 is replaced by the nominal bore, which the given drift already contains.

prompt.old: You are given only a drift value and asked whether a five and seven eighths inch packer will pass. What else do you need?
prompt.new: You are given only the drift of the single casing string a five and seven eighths inch packer will run through. What else do you need to say whether it passes?

2.old: The packer setting depth, since the quoted drift may not govern there.
2.new: The nominal bore of the casing, since the drift is deducted from it.

items.correct_change_reason: Correct option text unchanged; the prompt was sharpened to one casing string so the governing-drift question of the next tier no longer makes option 2 correct.

items.flag: twelve inch mandrel coverage depends on casing size (API drift mandrel lengths)
items.reason: API casing drift mandrel length varies with size, so a fixed twelve inch mandrel is not guaranteed for every joint; option 1 now names the standard mandrel for the pipe size.

1.old: A twelve inch mandrel passing through a new joint that has never been in a well.
1.new: The standard drift mandrel for that pipe size passing through a new joint never run in a well.

items.flag: near duplicate of beginner module m01-what-a-completion-is ord 14 (uncovered interval: skip and warn)
items.reason: Same concept and answer as the beginner m01 question; kept the beginner one and rewrote this into the l05 point that warnings catch missing data and never incorrect data.

prompt.old: What does the engine do when the profile does not cover an interval it is integrating?
prompt.new: A complete casing program is entered with a typo in one bore. What does the volume integration return?

explanation.old: The number that comes back is real and incomplete, and the warning is the only thing that says so.
explanation.new: Warnings catch missing data and nothing here catches incorrect data, so a complete program with a typo gives a complete profile, no warnings and a wrong volume.

0.old: It refuses the calculation and returns nothing, since a partial volume would mislead.
0.new: A refusal, since a bore that disagrees with the pipe tables fails validation before any integration starts.

1.old: It uses the bore of the nearest covered interval, which keeps the volume complete at the cost of a small unquantified error.
1.new: The volume over the correct intervals only, plus a warning naming the depths where the mistyped bore sits.

2.old: It returns the volume computed over the covered intervals only, with no indication that anything at all has been left out.
2.new: A volume built from the nearest valid catalog bore, since the engine replaces any bore it cannot match to a pipe size.

3.old: It skips the interval, continues, and adds a warning naming the depths.
3.new: A complete looking volume that is wrong, with an empty warning list.

items.correct_change_reason: Duplicate rewritten into a new question on the same lesson; answer_index kept at 3.
